articles.title: Don’t Mourn Hakeem Jeffries’s Speakership. Organize.
articles.author: Austin Warrington
articles.content_excerpt: In the wake of the midterms, the entirety of left-liberal America was jubilant. Democrats won majorities in the House and Senate, outperforming even the most idealistic predictions. But it was not only the Democratic victories that shocked observers — it was the kind of candidates who won. Democratic socialists had their strongest showing of any election in recent history, winning 169 endorsed ballot measures and seats at the local, state, and federal levels — their strongest showing of any general election in recent history. And the wins by nonsocialist progressives and even many centrists affirmed an agenda championed by democratic socialists, centering economic populism, wealth redistribution, and universal health care. articles.title: Anthropic Is Already Part of the Security Establishment
articles.author: Jacob Davis
articles.content_excerpt: Anthropic, which priced its initial public offering (IPO) last night and began trading on the Nasdaq today, published an S-1, the corporate prospectus for the offering. The document, which extends over five hundred pages, is intended to provide potential investors with an outline of its corporate structure, business model, and financial situation. Much of the document is, accordingly, dedicated to mundane legal minutiae: long lists of hypothetical events that might adversely affect investments, specific provisions for investment to comply with foreign nations’ securities law, etc. Some points, however, are quite instructive. articles.title: The Health Insurance Experience
articles.author: Rochester Red Star: News from Rochester DSA
articles.content_excerpt: by Sara C The following text is adapted from a speech delivered by Sara C at the NY Health Act Rally held October 17 at Rochester’s Liberty Pole. Despite health insurance being the primary way most Americans access any kind of health care, it’s not exactly popular. It can be expensive, not just in the premiums we pay for it with every paycheck, but also with deductibles that mean coverage doesn’t even start until you’ve paid a certain amount out of pocket. The coverage itself can be frustratingly limited. Beyond all that, health insurance companies have plenty of tactics to avoid payment and accountability. articles.title: How Will We Get People to Work Under Socialism?
articles.author: Nick French
articles.content_excerpt: With Zohran Mamdani’s rise to the mayoralty of the United States’s largest city and democratic socialists winning more and more elected offices at all levels across the country, there is renewed interest in and excitement about the idea of democratic socialism. But among socialists, there is little consensus on the content of that ideal. Many on the Left describe socialism in terms of greater income redistribution or an expanded public sector, with some socialists even describing their vision as compatible with capitalism. But we are seeing a growing number of proposals for feasible postcapitalist futures , distinct from both the social democratic welfare states and the state socialist systems of the twentieth century. articles.title: The Rising Congressional Left Is Positioned Well
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: In a bitter disappointment for the Left, Hakeem Jeffries — the vehemently pro-Israel Wall Street darling who once , bizarrely, did a version of George Wallace’s infamous “segregation forever” speech, only subbing in “Israel” for “segregation” — will be the next speaker of the House of Representatives. articles.author: Ja'Loni Owens
articles.content_excerpt: We talk about "kitchen table politics" as if it were a place free of culture, a neutral ground of gas prices and grocery bills where the culture wars are an unwelcome distraction. Anyone who has actually sat at one knows better. The kitchen table is where the culture war is fought, and it is fought by people who love you. articles.title: Rejecting Equality Is a Long-Standing American Tradition
articles.author: Robbie Nelson
articles.content_excerpt: Living in a country whose residents include both the world’s first trillionaire and 1.5 million homeless schoolchildren, the fact of American inequality is hard to miss. Such a reality produces countless justifications, explanations, and plans for ameliorating its worst impacts across the political spectrum. But at its sharpest edge, it also produces a coterie of intellectuals, pseudo-intellectuals, tycoons, activists, and posters who don’t merely attempt to explain or excuse inequality but rather celebrate its fruits and try to consolidate its bases. articles.title: The Violent Far-Right Response to France’s Protests
articles.author: Olly Haynes
articles.content_excerpt: For France’s media-political classes, the recent student movement has prompted a series of searching questions about violence and who has the right to use it. Debates often center on the alleged closeness of protesters to La France Insoumise, implying that Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s left-wing party is somehow responsible for vandalism by protesters and marginal acts of violence by students. Less remarked upon however, is that a wave of violence coming from the far right has also marked the protests and the presidential election campaign. Nor has it been much noted that this violence has killed already, and that Marine Le Pen’s Rassemblement National (RN) is alarmingly close to the violent groupuscules involved. articles.title: Why Are Most Union Leaders Silent on Booting Chuck Schumer?
articles.author: Eric Blanc
articles.content_excerpt: Why have only four national unions publicly backed Chris Van Hollen against Chuck Schumer for Senate leader? The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, the Office and Professional Employees International Union, National Nurses United, and the National Union of Healthcare Workers have taken Van Hollen’s side in this urgent fight. But where is everybody else? It’s hard to overstate the stakes. If Democrats once again squander the opportunity given to them by the American people, the lost chance to improve people’s lives — and the ensuing political backlash — could be even worse than what followed the Clinton, Obama, and Biden administrations. articles.title: Labor Mobilized for ‘Many vs. Mighty’ Midterms
articles.author: Jenny Brown
articles.content_excerpt: Something different was in the air as the labor movement mobilized for the midterms. More than usual, unions were willing to support insurgent candidates who refused corporate donations and bucked the Democratic Party establishment. They championed a Bernie Sanders-style list of working-class issues: Medicare for All, a higher minimum wage, union rights, immigrant rights, stopping war, and taxing the rich. Many are union members themselves. And they won. articles.title: ‘Delay, Deny, Discipline’ Is Amazon’s Real Pregnancy Policy, Workers Say
articles.author: Jenny Brown
articles.content_excerpt: Willamina Barclay was working as a picker at Amazon’s fulfillment center in Rochester, New York, when she felt lightheaded again. “She pleaded with a manager for a seat… He refused: ‘No, because you don’t have a [pregnancy] accommodation. If I give you a chair, I have to give everybody else a chair,’” he said, according to a recent lawsuit. But Barclay, who learned she was pregnant in March 2025, had already asked managers many times for accommodations—a seat, extra breaks to drink, eat, pee (or throw up) in the bathroom, no ladder-climbing or squatting, and no heavy lifting. Amazon—a company known for fast delivery—had failed to answer for weeks, demanding medical documentation.
